Perturbation family: a curve over a continuous data perturbation

Source: R/curve.R
stress_curve.Rd

Applies a user-supplied modification to the spec's data at each value of a continuous parameter, refits the pre-specified model and returns one row per value with the value in param. This generalises tipping-point searches that are not multiple-imputation based: assigning a contested participant a post-deviation trajectory, shifting one arm's observed values, moving a baseline definition, and so on. Rows are kind = "search" except the row at anchor, which is a counted alternative.

Usage

stress_curve(
  spec,
  values,
  modify,
  family = "perturbation curve",
  anchor = NULL,
  role = "sensitivity",
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

spec

A stress_spec().

values

Numeric vector of parameter values.

modify

A function function(data, value) returning a data frame in the spec's layout. It receives the spec's own data.

family

Family label for the rows.

anchor

The parameter value (if any) that represents an alternative analysis in its own right rather than a search point; NULL for none.

role

"sensitivity" or "supplementary"; see stress_fit().

cores

Number of worker processes; 1 fits sequentially.

Value

A stress_rows data frame, one row per value, with param set.

Examples

small <- mmrm::fev_data[mmrm::fev_data$USUBJID %in% paste0("PT", 1:60), ]
spec <- stress_spec(small, "FEV1", "USUBJID", "AVISIT", "ARMCD", "PBO", covariates = ~ FEV1_BL)
# shift every observed value of one subject on the active arm
shift_pt3 <- function(d, v) { k <- d$USUBJID == "PT3"; d$FEV1[k] <- d$FEV1[k] + v; d }
cv <- stress_curve(spec, values = c(-20, -10, 0, 10, 20), modify = shift_pt3, anchor = 0)
tipping_point(cv)
#>                                family n param_min param_max     p_min     p_max
#> perturbation curve perturbation curve 5       -20        20 0.1819731 0.4093701
#>                    crossing direction
#> perturbation curve       NA      <NA>
